prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1421; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a parking lot collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck while stationary. The claimant reports neck and back strain and is not represented by counsel, so all communication is going directly to the claimant.

Entry 2: Reviewed the first-notice statement. The claimant describes a rear impact at low speed in the lot, with the other vehicle backing into the claimant's car.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report and statements from two independent witnesses. Both confirm the collision happened as described and place the claimant inside the vehicle at the time.

Entry 4: Photos of the scene and the other driver's account match the claimant's description of the impact point and direction.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle damage. The rear bumper and trunk panel damage is consistent with the force and angle described in the reports.

Entry 6: Checked prior claims and records for this vehicle. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on file, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy's coverage start.

Entry 7: The claimant's medical records show the reported neck and back strain. No prior injury to the same body areas is known from available history, and the injury pattern fits the kind of force involved in this collision.

Entry 8: Claimant called to add a few details about the seating position and the moment of impact. The additional details are minor, and the core account has stayed the same since first notice.

Entry 9: Treatment has grown well beyond what this type of strain usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month. Requested treatment records and an independent medical review to look at the care plan.

Entry 10: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy. The file remains open pending the medical review and the bodily injury evaluation.
